identification.summary: Microsoft tracks Storm-0530 (formerly DEV-0530) as a North Korea-based actor that calls itself H0lyGh0st and runs ransomware operations using a payload of the same name [S1][S2]. Microsoft says it has used ransomware since June 2021 and compromised small businesses in multiple countries as early as September 2021 [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: June 2021 (first ransomware development and use); small-business compromises from September 2021 [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Name history: Microsoft's April 2023 update to its 2022 blog states DEV-0530 is now Storm-0530 and PLUTONIUM is now Onyx Sleet [S1]. Microsoft assesses Storm-0530 is connected to Onyx Sleet (PLUTONIUM, DarkSeoul, Andariel) but considers them distinct groups [S1][S2]. Do not merge Onyx Sleet or Symantec's Stonefly reporting into this record. Microsoft's profile page lists North Korea in its 'countries targeted' field, which conflicts with its victim description and looks like an error [S2].

attribution.sponsor: North Korea (assessed by Microsoft). Microsoft could not determine whether the North Korean government sponsors the activity or whether individuals are moonlighting for personal gain [S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft MSTIC assesses 'likely some overlap' with PLUTONIUM but considers the groups distinct because of differences in tempo, targeting and tradecraft [S1]. No government attribution to this cluster was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Microsoft cites DEV-0530 email accounts communicating with known PLUTONIUM accounts, shared infrastructure, custom malware controllers with similar names, use of tools created exclusively by PLUTONIUM, and activity most consistent with UTC+8 and UTC+9 time zones [S1][S2].

objectives: Primarily financial gain through ransomware and double extortion (encrypt files, steal a copy, threaten to publish or send data to victims' customers) [S1]. Microsoft notes state-sponsored cryptocurrency-targeting activity usually has broader victimology than seen here [S1].

targeting.notes: Victims were mainly small and midsize businesses and appeared to be targets of opportunity chosen seemingly at random [S1]. Several targets were compromised with HolyRS.exe in November 2021 [S1].

capabilities.summary: Initial access is suspected, not confirmed, to involve exploitation of CVE-2022-26352 (DotCMS remote code execution) on public-facing web applications and CMS; Microsoft observed no zero-days [S1]. Microsoft names two ransomware families: SiennaPurple (C++, BTLC_C.exe, first seen June 2021) and SiennaBlue (Go; HolyRS.exe, HolyLocker.exe, and BTLC.exe seen since April 2022), with RSA and AES encryption [S1]. BTLC.exe creates a scheduled task 'lockertask' running every minute as SYSTEM, falls back to a network share with hardcoded credentials if its server is unreachable, and obfuscates strings by subtracting 0x30 from each hex character [S1]. Victim data is exfiltrated before encryption, files are renamed to Base64 and given the .h0lyenc extension, a ransom note is dropped at C:\FOR_DECRYPT.html, and a data sample is emailed as proof [S1]. C2 observed at 193.56.29.123:8888 with access.php order parameters; contact via H0lyGh0st@mail2tor[.]com and a Tor leak site [S1]. Ransom demands were typically 1.2 to 5 Bitcoin, often negotiated down to under one-third; as of early July 2022 wallet analysis showed no successful payments [S1]. Microsoft also saw the group use tools created exclusively by Onyx Sleet [S2].

campaigns.name: H0lyGh0st ransomware development begins
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports ransomware development and use starting June 2021; the SiennaPurple variant BTLC_C.exe was first seen in this period.

campaigns.name: Early small-business compromises
campaigns.summary: Small businesses in multiple countries were compromised as early as September 2021.

campaigns.name: HolyRS.exe campaign
campaigns.summary: Several targets were compromised using the SiennaBlue variant HolyRS.exe.

campaigns.name: BTLC.exe variant appears
campaigns.summary: The latest Go-based SiennaBlue variant BTLC.exe has been seen since April 2022.

campaigns.name: Microsoft public disclosure
campaigns.summary: Microsoft publishes its analysis of DEV-0530, noting no successful ransom payments in observed wallets as of early July 2022.

campaigns.name: Renaming to Storm-0530
campaigns.summary: Microsoft updates its blog to state DEV-0530 is now Storm-0530 and PLUTONIUM is now Onyx Sleet.

diamond.adversary: North Korea-based actor self-styled H0lyGh0st, connected to Onyx Sleet; sponsorship unresolved [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Custom Go and C++ ransomware (SiennaBlue, SiennaPurple), double extortion, suspected DotCMS exploitation, Onyx Sleet tools [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: C2 IP 193.56.29.123:8888, Tor leak site, mail2tor email contact, ransom-note image on usaupload[.]com [S1].
diamond.victim: Small and midsize businesses in manufacturing, banking, education and event planning across multiple countries [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Mainly financial motive; no confirmed state tasking [S1].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing web applications and CMS (suspected DotCMS CVE-2022-26352) and Windows hosts [S1].

gaps: Microsoft could not determine state sponsorship versus moonlighting [S1].
CVE-2022-26352 as the initial access vector is suspected only [S1].
No Storm-0530 activity after July 2022 was found in the sources gathered; current status is unknown.
Victim countries and names are not public in the sources gathered [S1].

Relationship to Onyx Sleet/Andariel is assessed as overlap, not identity. Later government and vendor reporting on Andariel (including Symantec's Stonefly [S3]) concerns a different cluster and was not shown to cover H0lyGh0st.
Imported reference URLs (Kaspersky ICS CERT H2 2022 report, CISA AA23-040A, BlackBerry, Picus) could not be opened or confirmed to cover this actor; BlackBerry fetch failed and CISA is blocked.
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID is mapped for Storm-0530.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is internet-facing web applications and CMS at small and midsize organizations, including DoD-adjacent suppliers and local partners [S1]. STEP 2: The actor shows opportunistic targeting with a mainly financial motive, so risk is data theft, extortion and disruption rather than espionage [S1]. STEP 3: Template is public-facing app exploitation (suspected), data theft, scheduled-task persistence, encryption, then email and Tor-based extortion [S1]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic ransomware against small businesses. MDCOA is use of Onyx Sleet-built tools to move from financial extortion to higher-value targets, given the observed overlap [S1][S2]. Candidate indicators: scheduled task 'lockertask', .h0lyenc files, C:\FOR_DECRYPT.html, traffic to 193.56.29.123:8888 [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track small-business supplier incidents showing .h0lyenc or the ransom note and share IOCs [S1]. (2) Authorities: response at contractor networks runs through the DIB cybersecurity and DC3 channels rather than DoD direct action. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize patching of public-facing CMS and tested offline backups for exposed suppliers [S1]. (4) Coordination: because Microsoft sees links to Onyx Sleet, deconflict with analysts tracking Andariel before drawing conclusions about state tasking [S1][S2].

provenance.importedSummary: H0lyGh0st is a North Korean threat actor that has been active since June 2021. They are responsible for developing and deploying the H0lyGh0st ransomware, which targets small-to-medium businesses in various sectors. The group employs "double extortion" tactics, encrypting data and threatening to publish it if the ransom is not paid. There are connections between H0lyGh0st and the PLUTONIUM APT group, indicating a possible affiliation.
